_about: Ores across the map (docs/revisions/UPGRADE_PATHS_PLAN.md section 9, owner 2026-11-15). Read by scripts/science/ore_catalog.gd. Ore types: real Mars minerals from NASA's CRISM mineral list and the research note docs/revisions/research/mars_ores.md (kid names for ages 9-12). Deposits: Godot metres (x east, z south, y = ground height from data/terrain_height.res; the presenter snaps rocks to the ground anyway). Rings are measured from base_centre: near 0-80 m (few, small), middle 80-170 m, far 170-270 m (more and bigger). Placed by geology on our map: clays and carbonates in old low ground, ice on shaded north-facing slopes at the foot of the southern hills, meteorites and hematite on flat open plains, sulfates and silica on the rougher outer hills; every deposit is on ground with a slope under 13 degrees, reachable on foot from the base (no wall steeper than 32 degrees on the way), away from the base, the landing pad, the solar trackers and the comms dish. Totals (tuned 2026-11-15 against the ore costs in data/area_levels.json, which add up to 120 ore units over all tracks): 26 deposits, 76 units (near 12, middle 29, far 35), and each ore's units are about 60 % of what all upgrade levels ask for that ore (regolith 13/21, magnetite 7/11, hematite 17/28, olivine 4/7, silica 10/16, iron_meteorite 3/5, clay 5/9, sulfur 2/3, carbonate 3/5, gypsum 3/5, ice 4/6, sulfate 3/4; perchlorate 2, a hazard no upgrade uses), so the whole map pays for about 60 % of all upgrade levels. Re-tune the units here if the costs change. identify_lab_level: the lab level (AreaLevels track 'lab', missing = 1) at which the lab recognises a sample of this ore; the field engineer recognises every ore in the field.

middle.reach: drone V2 pre-scout, rover V2, a long suit walk

far.reach: drone V3-V4 scan, rover V3+ cabin, more science to identify

types.name: Basaltic regolith
types.what: The loose red-brown soil that covers almost all of Mars: crushed volcanic rock and dust.
types.found_by: every Mars rover and Mars Global Surveyor's TES

types.name: Magnetite
types.makes: iron (pulled out of the sand with a magnet)
types.what: Tiny black iron grains in the sand. A magnet picks them up.
types.found_where: Gale crater sandstones; a little in most Mars basalt

types.name: Hematite
types.makes: iron for metal parts (and oxygen when the iron is cleaned)
types.what: An iron mineral. On Mars it forms little grey beads the scientists call blueberries.
types.found_by: Mars Global Surveyor's TES and the Opportunity rover
types.found_where: Meridiani Planum, Aram Chaos and Vera Rubin Ridge

types.name: Iron-nickel meteorite
types.what: A lump of metal that fell from space. No melting needed: it is already metal.

types.name: Olivine
types.makes: magnesium and iron; it also soaks up CO2
types.what: A green mineral from volcanoes. Water breaks it down fast, so finding it shows the rock stayed dry.
types.found_by: Mars Global Surveyor's TES, MRO's CRISM and Perseverance's PIXL

types.name: Fe/Mg smectite clay
types.what: Soft clay that only forms in water. It still holds water inside it.
types.found_by: Mars Express OMEGA, MRO's CRISM and Curiosity's CheMin
types.found_where: Mawrth Vallis, Nili Fossae, Gale crater and the Jezero delta

types.name: Gypsum
types.makes: water (about a fifth of it is water) and plaster
types.what: A soft white mineral that forms when salty water dries up.
types.found_by: Mars Express OMEGA, MRO's CRISM and Curiosity
types.found_where: the north polar dunes and veins in Gale crater

types.name: Magnesium sulfates and jarosite
types.what: Yellowish salty layers left by old acidic water.
types.found_by: Mars Express OMEGA, MRO's CRISM and Opportunity
types.found_where: Valles Marineris, Meridiani Planum and Mount Sharp

types.name: Elemental sulfur
types.makes: sulfur concrete (a scientists' idea, not tried yet)
types.what: Bright yellow crystals of pure sulfur. Mars has only one known spot like this.
types.found_by: Curiosity (2024), when its wheel cracked open a rock

types.name: Carbonates
types.what: Rock that forms in lakes, like chalk and limestone on Earth. Acid makes it fizz.

types.name: Opaline silica / tridymite
types.what: Almost pure silica, the stuff glass is made of. It forms at old hot springs.
types.found_by: Spirit (Home Plate, about 91 % silica) and Curiosity's CheMin
types.found_where: Gusev crater, Gale crater (Buckskin) and Valles Marineris

types.name: Water ice
types.what: Real frozen water hiding just under the dust where the sun never shines.
types.found_by: MRO's SHARAD radar, Mars Odyssey's neutron spectrometer, HiRISE and Phoenix
types.found_where: the polar caps and buried ice in the mid-latitudes

types.name: Perchlorate salts
types.makes: oxygen (but it is poisonous: keep it sealed)
types.hazard_text: Danger salt: it is bad for people's thyroid. Keep it sealed in a sample bag and brush the suit off at the airlock.
types.what: A salt mixed into Mars soil. It is poisonous to people, but it holds lots of oxygen.
types.found_by: Phoenix's Wet Chemistry Lab (about half a percent of the soil) and Curiosity's SAM
types.found_where: the Phoenix landing site; probably all over Mars
